title: request-galley-annotated-compilation-jun-2026
content:
Summary:
This is a compact, customer-facing "request galley"—an annotated rollup of ~18 recent product asks surfaced by our CS reps during May–June 2026. Goal: provide engineering and product with a tight, action-oriented list (3 immediate micro-patches, 5 medium-term items, 2 strategic asks) plus context and friction evidence. This doc is intentionally terse: raw quotes, usage patterns, quick impact/effort scoring, owner suggestions, and next steps.

How this was compiled:
- Sources: post-call notes (CS rep notebooks), two customer interviews (Acme Analytics, LexiHealth), support tickets tagged "request" (n=43), and Slack thread #cs-field-ref (refs above).
- Method: group by user intent, surface concrete asks, map to probable area (hosted API, console, routing, billing), and flag risk/blocked items.

Representative customer quotes (verbatim snippets):
- "We lose tokens when streaming drops mid-generation—retries are brutal." — BrightCart (support-#987)
- "We need a way to pin a model variant for a route without changing app code for each rollout." — LexiHealth product lead
- "Batching suggestions feel like guesswork; we just want a rule-of-thumb and an auto-safe setting." — Acme Analytics

High-level themes (why this matters):
1) Reliability falls back into front-end complexity: customers want graceful client-visible failures and meaningful retry behavior.
2) Deployment control: enterprises want config-level model pinning and rollout controls per API route.
3) Cost tooling gaps: suggestions and automated configs for batching/quantization would reduce unit cost and lower support load.

Compact, prioritized asks (annotated):
A. Immediate micro-patches (target: 1–3 sprints)
  1) Streaming resume token behavior: return a deterministic resume token on partial responses + server-side idempotency window for 60s.
     - Evidence: 7 support tickets referencing partial-stream loss; one customer replaced Redwood because of noisy UX.
     - Quick impact: High (reduces churn, improves UX).
     - Effort estimate: Low–Medium (runtime + SDK change).
     - Suggested owner: eng-serving-runtime / SDK lead (ENGINF-789).
     - Quick link: add to JIRA CS-4123.
  2) Route-level model pin (console toggle + API route metadata): small UX + control plane change to pin model variant per route without code changes.
     - Evidence: LexiHealth, BrightCart ask; enterprise compliance constraint.
     - Impact: High for Dedicated/Private customers.
     - Effort: Medium.
     - Owner: product-hosted-api + console-and-rollouts.
  3) Batching suggestion helper: a console micro-card that inspects recent traffic patterns (seq length distribution) and recommends 3 safe configs (latency-sensitive / cost-balanced / throughput).
     - Evidence: repeated questions about how to choose batch sizes; several customers ran experiments and requested advice.
     - Impact: Medium (reduces CS time spent advising).
     - Effort: Low.
     - Owner: product-optimize + developer-experience.

B. Short-to-medium term (2–4 quarters)
  4) Prefix/KV cache visibility: expose per-route cache hit rates and opt-out rules in the Console; include per-token cost delta estimate.
     - Why: customers want to justify caching tradeoffs to finance and product teams.
     - Impact: High for cost-conscious customers.
     - Effort: Medium–High.
     - Owner: console-and-rollouts + observability.
  5) Canary rollouts with deterministic fallback: allow 0–100% split with automatic fallback when tail latency or error-rate exceed thresholds for 5 consecutive minutes.
     - Evidence: Platform teams want predictable rollout without writing bespoke code.
     - Impact: High.
     - Effort: Medium.
     - Owner: product-hosted-api + platform-engineering.
  6) Billing attribution line-items for quantized variants: show per-request/route per-model-variant cost estimate to allow teams to measure savings of quantized runs.
     - Impact: Medium.
     - Effort: Medium.
     - Owner: finance-and-legal + product-optimize.
  7) Improved error codes and doc mapping: map transient vs permanent server errors, suggested client mitigation.
     - Impact: Medium.
     - Effort: Low.
     - Owner: developer-experience.

C. Strategic / product bets (6–12 months)
  8) Auto-tune optimizer: ML-driven suggestion engine that tunes batching + cache + quantization per workload and can propose an optional auto-apply mode.
     - Impact: Very High (could be a paid Optimize add-on).
     - Effort: High.
     - Owner: product-optimize + applied-ml.
  9) Private/VPC first-class audit mode: deeper audit trails + KMS rotation help for Private customers on regulated workloads.
     - Impact: High for enterprise closed deals.
     - Effort: High.
     - Owner: private-deployments + security-and-compliance.

Quick impact/effort table (verbal):
- Low effort, high impact: streaming resume token, batching suggestion helper, improved error codes.
- Medium effort, high impact: route-level pin, canary rollouts, cache visibility.
- High effort, high impact: auto-tune optimizer, private audit mode.

Risk flags / things to validate before prioritizing:
- Some asks (e.g., resume tokens) interact with legal/customer data retention for Private deployments — check with security/compliance before broad rollout.
- Cost estimation surfaces may be noisy if we do not normalize per-token accounting across quantized vs full variants.
- Any auto-apply optimizer must have a safe rollback and opt-out per route to avoid surprising customers.

Concrete next steps (owner, ETA):
- Triage meeting: CS + Eng + Product on 2026-07-02 to convert A.1–A.3 into scoped tickets (owner: Marcel Nguyen).
- Create engineering spike for resume-token UX/semantics (owner: Oliver Park, ETA: 2 weeks).
- Product to scope console micro-card for batching suggestions (owner: Sofia Mendes, ETA: 3 weeks).
- Add priority labels on JIRA: tag CS-4123 with "cs-priority=high" and link ENGINF-789.

Back-of-envelope metrics to watch (if implemented):
- Support ticket volume referencing streaming loss (target: -80% over 3 months)
- Customer satisfaction score for onboarding (target: +0.2 NPS lift for Dedicated customers)
- Average per-request token cost variance after batching suggestions (target: -12% for selected workloads)

Open questions for discussion at triage:
- Do we prefer a conservative resume-token semantics (server replays last full chunk) vs a more aggressive partial-resume with server-side reconciliation?
- For the batching console suggestion, how much historical window is acceptable (1h/24h/7d) to produce stable suggestions?
- Should the auto-tune optimizer be an opt-in preview with usage credits?

Appendix: short ticket stubs / references (examples to copy into JIRA templates)
- CS-STREAM-RESUME: "Streaming resume token + SDK-safe retry window" — copy evidence from support tickets 987, 1123, 1201.
- CS-ROUTE-PIN: "Route-level model pinning and console toggle" — attach LexiHealth email chain.
- CS-BATCH-HINT: "Console micro-card: batching/latency presets" — attach Acme Analytics experiment logs.

Notes to self / informal:
- We should run a quick survey of 10 high-usage customers to quantify preference for auto-apply vs suggestion-only.
- Slack: pull the thread with BrightCart engineer (link above) to add a short transcript as evidence.
- If product wants, I can build the initial batching-card mock (1 day) to reduce ambiguity in the triage meeting.

End of rollup.
